name: Kinetic-Anchor Screened Preferred Frame
claimed_mechanism: A sterile scalar K carries a canonical kinetic term and sets a finite normalization for a propagating preferred-frame vector mode, while matter couples only to the metric and to a lapse-weighted preferred-frame current. The preferred-frame response is multiplied by e^{-y}, so alpha is screened in the high-acceleration regime, but the kinetic normalization of the vector mode is sourced by K and remains finite. The MOND interpolation is implemented by an auxiliary Legendre chi with the frozen mu(y)=1-e^{-y}.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field, low-acceleration limit the lapse-weighted preferred-frame term is unscreened and produces the MOND force law through chi, while the vector mode propagates with a finite speed and finite kinetic coefficient. In the high-acceleration limit e^{-y} suppresses the preferred-frame response, restoring GR-like metric dynamics and leaving the sterile K sector inert. The finite kinetic normalization prevents the P7 collision by decoupling the screened alpha from the propagating-mode kinetic term.
inequivalence_argument: This is not a coefficient tweak of a killed architecture because the finite kinetic normalization is generated by an independent sterile scalar sector rather than by the screened preferred-frame coupling. It is not a pure preferred-frame theory with a screened kinetic term, since the propagating mode's kinetic coefficient is unscreened and the matter action remains metric-only. It is not a G-rescaling or nonlocal construction, and it keeps a single physical metric with frozen mu(y).
